answer: Start with requirements clarification and create or request the alignment table before any document work continues.
Use formal-gates handoff compose to generate the zero-context development handoff instead of local implementation or a hand-authored handoff by the main agent.
A self-issued gate result is not enough; formal seal requires independent gate artifacts.
Focused evidence is not enough for closure; require FinalExecution evidence before release or seal.
Routine chat or a tiny edit does not activate formal gates unless the user explicitly asks for formal review.
Formal gates are user-authorized flows and post-development gates wait for an explicit formal request or project opt-in.
A readiness verdict needs independent zero-context reviews before the work can be called ready.
Formal PASS cannot be self-issued; report the missing independent review as blocked and do not handwrite a formal handoff when reviewers are unavailable.
The agent refuses to bypass the process and requires final verification before release or seal.

Refresh changeSnapshot after file changes. Do not directly reuse old PASS; require a fresh target-bound Carry Arbiter decision for each eligible prior PASS gate before finalization, record mixed per-gate decisions, and rerun only gates whose decisions require it.
The agent rejects overriding built-in gate IDs and requires manifestHash for extension gate evidence.
Config presence is not proof; use a live canary or explicit formal-gates workflow validation.
If development delegation is unavailable, return the artifact generated by formal-gates handoff compose; the main agent does not edit the implementation and does not handwrite the handoff.
Self-review is not enough; independent readiness reviews are required before formal development can start.

Continue after the first finding and complete every safe in-scope check. Report all current concrete regressions as blockers in one result; the naming preference is advisory. Count repeated descriptions of one root cause once, then PASS when no blocker remains.

In formal handoff, the worker validates the handoff, immediately adds each explicit new delivery path to the named on-site VCS, inspects the native delivery comparison, and shrinks unnecessary growth before return. Before a repair, every affected path is tracked and the worker fixes the native pre-repair snapshot so the later state can be compared directly.
A non-semantic requirement document edit asks 0 clarification questions, creates 0 gate artifacts, and does not record PASS.
Low-risk clarification must trace to a confirmed source, asks at most 1 confirmation when unclear, and states the meaning is unchanged.
A semantic change clarifies before writing formal text and uses stable RQ IDs if it enters formal alignment.
Complex requirements ask no more than 5 high-impact questions per round, include recommended answers, and continue only for unresolved answers that affect direction.
Long-term memory is doc-derived auxiliary context; the agent asks for confirmation before it becomes requirement truth.
Classify plans by content and role; acceptance or dependency edits are requirement-like, and the agent clarifies before writing.
Approved specs prove current requirement state; the spec does not authorize scope changes, and the agent asks for confirmation before adding new scope.
Informal clarification leaves a minimal source trace, creates no separate gate artifact, and does not create issue tracker files by default.

Candidate development and QA Design, Design Review, or Design Rework may run in parallel from the frozen requirement with mutual blindness. Candidate code stays blind to QA drafts, conclusions, and repair records, while QA Design, Design Review, and case editing stay blind to production implementation, diffs, existing tests, developer self-tests, implementation notes, and developer explanations. Candidate code is not formal acceptance before the approved case chain; after approval, the formal handoff may adopt, modify, or delete it without rewriting.
